headline: 3 jailed after rampage at New Gini Properties and Salman Muqtadir's studio
summary: Attackers fired 50 rounds and looted property worth Tk 29 million from a housing project and a content creator's studio in Dhaka.
details: A Dhaka court has sent three people to jail following their arrest for vandalism, looting, and theft at the New Gini Properties housing project in South Manikdi. The suspects, identified as Md Mamun, Md Aslam, and Md Munna, face a remand hearing on Wednesday.

The attack occurred around 10:30pm on Saturday, targeting the project office and a studio named 'Brownfish' belonging to content creator Salman Muqtadir. Police believe the incident may have stemmed from a land dispute between a property developer and a retired military officer.

Approximately 50 attackers entered the project, firing around 50 rounds of gunfire and using machetes, daggers, and sticks. Several people, including site engineer Md Parvez, were severely injured during the assault.

The assailants looted cash, laptops, computers, electrical cables, cameras, and professional media equipment. New Gini Properties claimed damages worth Tk 14 million and theft of property worth Tk 15 million.
When Cantonment Police arrived, the attackers opened fire on them, prompting officers to fire five shotgun rounds in self-defence to control the situation.
Police arrested two suspects at the scene and a third in a follow-up operation, recovering local weapons and spent bullet casings from the arrestees.
caption:
50 attackers, 50 rounds of gunfire, and Tk 29 million in losses. A midnight rampage in Dhaka leaves a studio and housing project in ruins.

A Dhaka court has sent three people to jail following their arrest for vandalism, looting, and theft at the New Gini Properties housing project in South Manikdi. The suspects, identified as Md Mamun, Md Aslam, and Md Munna, face a remand hearing on Wednesday.

The attack occurred around 10:30pm on Saturday, targeting the project office and a studio named 'Brownfish' belonging to content creator Salman Muqtadir. Police believe the incident may have stemmed from a land dispute between a property developer and a retired military officer.

Approximately 50 attackers entered the project, firing around 50 rounds of gunfire and using machetes, daggers, and sticks. Several people, including site engineer Md Parvez, were severely injured during the assault.

The assailants looted cash, laptops, computers, electrical cables, cameras, and professional media equipment. New Gini Properties claimed damages worth Tk 14 million and theft of property worth Tk 15 million.

When Cantonment Police arrived, the attackers opened fire on them, prompting officers to fire five shotgun rounds in self-defence to control the situation.

Police arrested two suspects at the scene and a third in a follow-up operation, recovering local weapons and spent bullet casings from the arrestees.

headline_marked: 5 [[arrested near US military base]] in UK
headline: 5 arrested near US military base in UK
summary: British police detained five suspects suspects suspected of planning 'significant harm' to the RAF Fairford base, leading to the evacuation of 85 homes.
details: British police arrested five people near a US military airbase in the UK, suspected of planning a major attack. The arrests occurred after police received a tip-off about three suspicious vans heading toward the RAF Fairford base.
US President Donald Trump praised the 'extraordinary work' of British and US authorities, stating that the suspects were being monitored and were planning to cause 'significant harm' to the base.

As a precautionary measure, residents of 85 homes in a nearby village were evacuated early in the morning. A 400-meter security perimeter was established, and bomb disposal units examined the suspicious vehicles.
The incident occurs amid heightened tensions, as the UK government has permitted the US to use RAF Fairford to launch attacks on Iranian missile sites in the Strait of Hormuz.
Security has been increased at other US-operated bases in the UK, including RAF Lakenheath, where armored vehicles and soldiers were seen at the entrance.
British authorities have also expressed growing concern over potential sabotage and cyberattacks, particularly following warnings about Russian threats to critical infrastructure.
caption:
Five people arrested near a US military base in the UK after planning 'significant harm'. 85 homes evacuated.

British police arrested five people near a US military airbase in the UK, suspected of planning a major attack. The arrests occurred after police received a tip-off about three suspicious vans heading toward the RAF Fairford base.

US President Donald Trump praised the 'extraordinary work' of British and US authorities, stating that the suspects were being monitored and were planning to cause 'significant harm' to the base.

As a precautionary measure, residents of 85 homes in a nearby village were evacuated early in the morning. A 400-meter security perimeter was established, and bomb disposal units examined the suspicious vehicles.

The incident occurs amid heightened tensions, as the UK government has permitted the US to use RAF Fairford to launch attacks on Iranian missile sites in the Strait of Hormuz.

Security has been increased at other US-operated bases in the UK, including RAF Lakenheath, where armored vehicles and soldiers were seen at the entrance.

British authorities have also expressed growing concern over potential sabotage and cyberattacks, particularly following warnings about Russian threats to critical infrastructure.
